# Six-input worksheet and claim audit

Original editable worksheet. Complete it from correspondence and your own dated factual notes. Keep the original excerpts alongside the draft. Do not use an AI-generated summary as a source. Use only material you may share with your chosen AI provider; redact private details.

## Six drafting inputs

1. Recipient and relationship: [name, role, relationship; source label]
2. Earlier events: [what you wrote/discussed, exact date, source label and original excerpt; unknowns]
3. One current request: [one question/action you want the recipient to answer]
4. Tone: [e.g. neutral, warm, concise; avoid blame]
5. Hard facts: [verified names, topic, options, dates, actual commitments and constraints, each with a source label; list missing facts explicitly]
6. Exclusions: [e.g. no assumed agreement, invented deadline, delivery/read claim, reason for silence or new commitment]

## Original source pack

Repeat this block for each source. Paste enough context to preserve qualifications or contradictory wording; labels or URLs alone are insufficient.

- Source label: [S1]
- Source type and author: [earlier email / your dated note; name]
- Date and relevant timezone: [known value or UNKNOWN]
- Original redacted text:

```text
[Paste actual relevant text, including subject/date/sender where useful.]
```

- Missing information/conflicts: [state them; do not fill them in]

## Draft to audit

Audience and purpose: [recipient and one requested action]

```text
[Paste the whole chosen draft, including subject, greeting and signature.]
```

Supply this draft and the ORIGINAL source pack to the complementary claim-audit prompt. The primary prompt's “Facts I supplied” output is not independent evidence. If the source pack is missing or too short, add substantive excerpts or stop the audit; do not invent support.

## Claim-to-source comparison

Use the audit's returned status where applicable and describe the gap in plain English. A traceable source can itself be wrong. The model does not verify reality or open source links. Split sentences with multiple assertions into separate rows.

| Exact draft assertion | Source label and exact excerpt | Gap / audit status | Human correction | Approved final wording |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Assertion] | [S1: exact words, or no matching excerpt] | [Supported by supplied text / unsupported / conflict / unclear] | [Keep / remove / soften / ask] | [Text or removed] |

A pure request or thanks need not be a factual assertion. Review its clarity and tone separately; do not manufacture a SOURCED row for it. A request can still contain a claim: “by the deadline you gave me” asserts a previous deadline and needs evidence.

## Human final

```text
[Write the corrected email here; remove source codes and unresolved placeholders from the recipient-facing message.]
```

- [ ] Every factual assertion agrees with its original excerpt, including names/dates.
- [ ] No agreement, urgency, deadline or receipt/read status is inferred.
- [ ] One clear request; no blame or speculation about silence.
- [ ] Recipients, thread, signature, confidentiality and any actual attachment checked.
- [ ] All placeholders removed; final review completed by [name] on [date].

Keep your audit with your notes. Decide separately whether and when to send; neither prompt sends anything.
